text.p: BLANTYRE, Nov 6 (Reuter) These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The United Council for Dialogue (UCD), a group of nine opposition parties not represented in parliament, on Tuesday called for the formation of a "truth commission" to investigate human rights abuses during former president Kamuzu Banda's 30-year-rule.
- Among the incidents that they would want probed are the killings of human rights activists allegedly at the hands of government agents.

- Police in Northern Malawi on Sunday ambushed a five-member gang hours after it robbed British cyclist Christopher Samuel who is on a cycle tour of the world. Police arrested two members of the gang and recovered most of Samuel's property. He was on his way to South Africa from Tanzania.

- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) on Tuesday nominated new candidates to replace earlier choices for the November 19 by-elections in Blantyre's Ndirande township and Machinga districts. One candidate has been dropped for failing to register as voter, and another has offered to withdraw.

- The chairman of the United Council for Dialogue (UCD) on Tuesday accused President Bakili Muluzi of being insensitive to other people's illnesses. At the weekend Muluzi called UCD leaders "epileptic victims who would fade".
- Press Bakeries staff, a division of the country's biggest conglomerate, Press Corporation, have boycotted work in protest against alleged racist remarks by a manager.
